s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic bone pain with progressive worsening and multi-system involvement
salient_findings: Diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
Mild thrombocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old man with no prior medical history
4-year history of diffuse bone pain
Bone pain worsened over the past 2 months
Developed blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
Previous workups were nondiagnostic
Treated with analgesics, vitamin D, topical steroids, and antihistamines
Normal white-cell count and differential
Normal hemoglobin
Mild thrombocytosis
Normal renal and liver function tests
Negative tumor markers and autoimmune serologies
Mildly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on knee radiographs
Intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri on humeral radiographs
Sclerosis of the proximal ulnae and radii on forearm radiographs
Bilateral symmetric uptake on 99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI of the lower limbs
Enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues on MRI
FDG-avid lesions on PET/CT of the brain
Bilateral perinephric soft-tissue thickening with FDG uptake on CT and PET/CT of the abdomen
CT-guided biopsy of the left proximal tibia showed diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis

Tuberous sclerosis complex with bone lesions
per_call: Diaphyseal medullary stenosis with bone sclerosis
Tuberous sclerosis complex with bone lesions

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells on biopsy, consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and histiocytic infiltration, although immunohistochemical staining pattern is not typical for Langerhans cell histiocytosis

shortlist.label: Sclerosteosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sclerotic bone changes and symmetric uptake on bone scintigraphy, consistent with sclerosteosis

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and sclerotic changes, although the presence of foamy histiocytes and fibrosis is not typical for Paget's disease

shortlist.label: Melorheostosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sclerotic bone changes and multifocal intramedullary sclerosis, consistent with melorheostosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs, and multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI, along with the presence of foamy histiocytes and fibrosis on biopsy, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease. The disease is also known to involve extraskeletal sites, such as the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues, as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The biopsy showed histiocytes negative for CD1a, S100, and langerin, which are typically positive in Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Sclerosteosis
rejected.why: Sclerosteosis is a rare genetic disorder that typically presents with skeletal abnormalities, but it does not typically involve the extraskeletal sites seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Paget's disease of bone
rejected.why: Paget's disease of bone typically presents with an abnormal bone remodeling process, which is not consistent with the biopsy findings in this patient.

rejected.label: Melorheostosis
rejected.why: Melorheostosis is a rare bone disorder that typically presents with a 'dripping candle wax' appearance on radiographs, which is not seen in this patient.
